_note: Round 12 (E): the regulars. Each has a face (sim-core avatarFor on their id, in their own clothes colour), a job, a favourite dish and five beats: an intro (their first visit, on an open day) and four VIP orders. A VIP order names one of `dishes` and a weekday; it is met on that weekday when the dish sold and the night averaged at least 3.5 stars. A beat with `bad` also moves on after a poorer night (the story branches; no photo); a beat without one waits for next week. Everything is worked out from the seed and the day results by packages/game/src/lib/regulars.ts; the sim never reads this file. Dish ids are all from the starter library.

regulars.name: Priya Nair
regulars.intro: Priya came in alone with a paperback and ordered the katsu without looking at the menu. She'll be back. She has the look.

beats.order: {name} has a first date on {weekday} and wants the {dish}: 'the one thing I can't spill down myself'.
beats.good: The date went brilliantly. They split a pudding. Nobody splits a pudding on a bad date.
beats.bad: The date talked about his car for an hour. Priya ate the {dish} in silence and says it was the best part of the night.

photo.caption: Two forks, one pudding

beats.gossip: Love is in the air at {restaurant}: a first date on {weekday} went so well they shared a pudding. Two spoons. Disgusting. Lovely.

beats.order: {name} wants a table for two on {weekday}. Second date, or a brand-new one: she won't say. Just make sure the {dish} is on.
beats.good: Date number two. She's started saying 'we'. The {dish} has been named 'our dish'. Steady on.
beats.bad: It turned out he hates sharing food. Priya has decided she is 'focusing on her career now'.

photo.caption: A blurry selfie by the window

beats.gossip: Sources at {restaurant} confirm a second date went well. The {dish} is now 'their dish'. Brace yourselves, {district}.

beats.order: {name} is bringing her mum on {weekday} to 'meet the restaurant'. It's a test. The {dish} is the test.
beats.good: Priya's mum asked for the recipe, which is the highest honour a mum can give. Priya looked very relieved.

photo.caption: Priya and her mum, both pointing at the pudding menu

beats.gossip: A mum at {restaurant} on {weekday} asked for a recipe. In mum terms, that's five stars.

beats.order: {name} has news and wants to tell everyone over the {dish} on {weekday}. She's practising her surprised face.
beats.good: She's been promoted to practice manager. The whole table cheered. A man at the next table cheered too, for no reason.

photo.caption: Priya's promotion night

beats.gossip: Congratulations to Priya, newly promoted, who celebrated at {restaurant} with a {dish}. We don't know her. We're proud anyway.

regulars.name: Marcus Webb
regulars.intro: Marcus came in looking at his phone, sighed at his phone, and ordered a burger. His phone is the problem, we suspect.

beats.order: {name} has been dumped by text. He's coming in on {weekday} to eat the {dish} and 'process'.
beats.good: He arrived heartbroken and left with a full stomach and a plan. The plan is 'get a new phone'. Progress.
beats.bad: The night was slow and so was the food. He read old messages over the {dish}. Somebody take his phone.

photo.caption: Marcus's phone, face down. A brave choice.

beats.gossip: Heartbreak at table four on {weekday}. Marcus, if you're listening: the {dish} believes in you.

beats.order: {name}'s ex wants to 'talk' on {weekday}. He's picked {restaurant} for the moral support. And the {dish}.
beats.good: They agreed to be friends. Actual friends. She even let him have the last bit of the {dish}.
beats.bad: They did not agree to be friends. She took the last of the {dish}. Marcus says that's 'exactly the problem'.

photo.caption: A handshake. Awkward, but a handshake.

beats.gossip: Peace talks at {restaurant} on {weekday}. A break-up has become a friendship. The {dish} brokered the deal.

beats.order: {name} has started running. He's rewarding himself with the {dish} on {weekday}, which rather undoes the running.
beats.good: He ran five kilometres and ate one {dish}. He says it's 'balance'. We say it's lunch.

photo.caption: Muddy trainers under table four

beats.gossip: Marcus from table four ran his first five kilometres this week. He celebrated with the {dish}. Balance.

beats.order: {name} met someone at the Saturday run. He wants to bring her on {weekday}. The {dish}, and no phones.
beats.good: Two phones stayed in two pockets all night. They talked about running for three hours. They're perfect for each other.

photo.caption: Marcus and Jo, both in running tops, both very pleased

beats.gossip: Remember Marcus, dumped by text? He's met someone. At a run. On purpose. Good lad.

regulars.name: Dev Okafor
regulars.intro: Dev photographed his ramen from four angles, then didn't post any of them. He used to run a food blog. He doesn't talk about it.

beats.order: {name} is thinking of starting his blog again. He's 'testing' himself on the {dish} on {weekday}.
beats.good: He wrote three paragraphs on the {dish} on a napkin and didn't throw it away. That's the first post.
beats.bad: The food was slow and he wrote 'meh' on a napkin. He crossed it out. 'Too harsh,' he said. 'I've been there.'

photo.caption: A napkin with very small handwriting

beats.gossip: Food blogger Dev Okafor is back! He wrote about the {dish} at {restaurant} on a napkin. It's online now. The napkin is framed.

beats.order: {name} needs a 'big' post for the relaunch. He'd like the {dish} on {weekday}, lit nicely.
beats.good: The relaunch post has a hundred readers. Ninety-nine are strangers. One is his mum, who commented 'lovely'.

photo.caption: Dev's blog, open on a laptop, on table six

beats.gossip: Dev's blog is back with a post about {restaurant}'s {dish}. His mum says it's lovely. She's right.

beats.order: {name} has heard {blogger} might be about. He wants the {dish} on {weekday} 'to see how a professional does it'.
beats.good: He worked out that {blogger} never writes the word 'delicious'. He's banned it from his blog too. It's harder than it sounds.
beats.bad: He tried to review the {dish} like {blogger} would and made himself sad. 'She's rude,' he said, 'but she's right.'

photo.caption: Dev taking notes on someone else's notes

beats.gossip: Dev Okafor has banned the word 'delicious' from his blog. Bold. Tasty. Er, flavourful.

beats.order: {name} is celebrating a thousand readers with the {dish} on {weekday}. Same table as the first time.
beats.good: A thousand readers. And this morning, a follow from {blogger}. Dev hasn't stopped smiling. It's slightly worrying.

photo.caption: Same table, same ramen, a thousand readers

beats.gossip: Dev Okafor's comeback is complete: a thousand readers and a follow from {blogger}. He celebrated at {restaurant}. Of course he did.

regulars.name: Ellie Chen
regulars.intro: Ellie spread revision cards over the whole table and ordered mac & cheese 'for brain power'. The science on that is unclear.

beats.order: {name} has mock exams. She wants to revise over the {dish} on {weekday}. Quiet table, please.
beats.good: She learned the whole of the water cycle between two forkfuls. The {dish} is now officially study food.
beats.bad: It was too noisy to think. She learned one fact about glaciers and dropped cheese on it.

photo.caption: Revision cards, slightly cheesy

beats.gossip: Exam season on {district}: a student revised the water cycle over the {dish} at {restaurant} on {weekday}. It rained. Topical.

beats.order: {name}'s friends want in. Five of them, {weekday}, the {dish}, and a promise to 'actually revise'.
beats.good: They actually revised. For eleven minutes. Then they quizzed each other on the menu. Ellie won.

photo.caption: Five people, one highlighter

beats.gossip: A study group at {restaurant} on {weekday} revised for eleven whole minutes. A record for {district}.

beats.order: {name} has her last exam on {weekday} morning. She'd like the {dish} the night before 'for luck'.
beats.good: She ate, went home and slept nine hours. The exam had a question on glaciers. She knew it.
beats.bad: Dinner ran late and she got home after ten. She says the exam was 'fine'. Teenagers say 'fine' about everything.

photo.caption: A four-leaf clover drawn on a napkin

beats.gossip: Good luck to every student on {district} with exams this week. One of them prepared with the {dish}. Science.

beats.order: Results day! {name} wants the {dish} on {weekday}, whatever the envelope says.
beats.good: Top grades. She opened the envelope at the table and screamed. So did the people at table three, on her behalf.

photo.caption: Ellie, an envelope and a very tall {dish}

beats.gossip: Results day joy at {restaurant}: one student, top grades, one {dish} the size of her head.

regulars.name: Arthur Pembridge
regulars.intro: Arthur sat by the window, set his watch by the clock on the wall, and told the server it was two minutes slow. It was.

beats.order: {name}'s granddaughter is 'scouting' for his ninetieth. She's coming on {weekday} to try the {dish}.
beats.good: She's booked the long table. 'Grandad will love it,' she said. 'He'll say he doesn't. He will.'

photo.caption: A booking, written in very large letters

beats.gossip: Big birthday coming at {restaurant}: someone on {district} is about to turn ninety. Practise your singing.

beats.order: {name} insists on a 'test run' of the {dish} on {weekday}. He doesn't trust anything he hasn't tested.
beats.good: He ate every bit, checked his watch and said, 'Adequate.' His granddaughter says that's his highest mark ever.
beats.bad: The {dish} took ages. He timed it. He'll mention it. For years.

photo.caption: Arthur's pocket watch, open on the table

beats.gossip: A retired train driver called the {dish} at {restaurant} 'adequate' on {weekday}. Locals say that's a rave review.

beats.order: The ninetieth! Fourteen of the family on {weekday}. Arthur wants the {dish}. The cake is a secret.
beats.good: Fourteen people sang. Arthur pretended to hate it and wiped his eyes 'because of the candles'.
beats.bad: The cake arrived before the mains. Arthur ate it anyway. 'At ninety,' he said, 'pudding first is allowed.'

photo.caption: Ninety candles (well, a nine and a zero)

beats.gossip: Happy ninetieth, Arthur! Fourteen people sang at {restaurant} on {weekday}. Arthur says he didn't cry. Arthur cried.

beats.order: {name} would like 'his' table on {weekday}, the {dish}, and for nobody to make a fuss. Make a small fuss.
beats.good: Same table, same time, a small fuss. He's booked every {weekday} for the rest of the year.

photo.caption: A model train, left 'for the window'

beats.gossip: Arthur, ninety, has a standing booking at {restaurant} every {weekday}. The table has a little brass train on it now.

regulars.name: Sandy Okoye
regulars.intro: Sandy parked her food truck, Wheely Good Food, outside, came in, and ordered 'whatever's your bestseller'. Checking out the competition, we reckon.

beats.order: {name} wants to taste your {dish} on {weekday}. 'For research,' she says, meaning nicking ideas.
beats.good: She ate it, nodded slowly, and wrote 'they're good' on her hand. Professional respect.

photo.caption: Wheely Good Food, parked a bit too close

beats.gossip: The food truck parked on {district} has been 'researching' the {dish} at {restaurant}. Imitation is flattery. Or theft.

beats.order: {name} is thinking of selling the truck. She'd like to think about it over the {dish} on {weekday}.
beats.good: She made a list: 'sell' on one side, 'keep' on the other. 'Keep' has one word on it: 'freedom'. She's still thinking.
beats.bad: A slow night at the restaurant made her miss her own slow nights. 'At least the truck has wheels,' she said.

photo.caption: A list, mostly crossings-out

beats.gossip: Rumour on {district}: the Wheely Good Food truck could be for sale. Sandy was seen thinking hard over a {dish}.

beats.order: A buyer is meeting {name} on {weekday}. Neutral ground, she says. Your {dish} is the neutral ground.
beats.good: The buyer offered a good price. Sandy shook his hand, then said she'd 'sleep on it'. She's slept on it six times.
beats.bad: The buyer complained about the {dish} for ten minutes. Sandy decided she wouldn't sell him a sandwich, let alone a truck.

photo.caption: An offer, written on the back of a menu

beats.gossip: Big deal over lunch at {restaurant} on {weekday}: a food truck might be changing hands. Sandy says nothing. Loudly.

beats.order: {name} has decided. She'll tell you over the {dish} on {weekday}. She's grinning, which is either good or terrifying.
beats.good: She's keeping the truck, and parking it outside {restaurant} on Saturdays: 'You do the sit-down, I'll do the queue.' A deal.

photo.caption: Sandy and the truck, staying put

beats.gossip: Wheely Good Food is staying on {district}! Sandy will park by {restaurant} on Saturdays. The queues are going to be enormous.

regulars.name: Ray Duffy
regulars.intro: Ray ordered the all-day breakfast at seven in the evening. 'My day started at four,' he said. Fair.

beats.order: {name} is writing a novel about a bus driver. He'd like to 'work on chapter one' over the {dish} on {weekday}.
beats.good: Chapter one is done. The bus driver is called Roy. Roy is definitely not Ray. Roy also loves the {dish}.

photo.caption: Chapter one, page one, a gravy stain

beats.gossip: A local bus driver is writing a novel at {restaurant}. The hero is a bus driver. Bold choice.

beats.order: {name} is stuck on chapter seven. He wants the {dish} on {weekday} and 'no plot twists, please'.
beats.good: He got Roy through chapter seven by sending him down a diversion. 'Like life,' Ray said. Deep.
beats.bad: The night was chaos and Ray wrote it all down. Chapter seven is now about a restaurant. Uh oh.

photo.caption: A bus ticket used as a bookmark

beats.gossip: Chapter seven of the bus novel was written at {restaurant} on {weekday}. Ray says it has 'a twist'. It's a diversion.

beats.order: {name} is reading chapter one to his book club on {weekday}. They're coming for the {dish}. He's terrified.
beats.good: The book club laughed in all the right places and none of the wrong ones. Ray had to go outside for a minute.

photo.caption: Ray, reading, holding the page very tight

beats.gossip: The {district} book club heard the first chapter of a bus driver's novel at {restaurant}. Reviews: 'fun', 'loud', 'more Roy'.

beats.order: A publisher wrote back to {name}! He's celebrating with the {dish} on {weekday}. His treat. Very much his treat.
beats.good: They want the book. Roy goes to print next spring. There's a scene set in a restaurant that looks a lot like this one.

photo.caption: A signed copy, 'for the kitchen'

beats.gossip: Ray from the number 42 is getting his novel published. There's a restaurant in it. Somebody check it's a nice one.

regulars.name: Bola Adeyemi
regulars.intro: Bola came in still in scrubs, ate a curry in eleven minutes flat and thanked everyone like they'd saved her life. It's usually the other way round.

beats.order: {name} has a promotion interview on {weekday}. She'd like the {dish} and five quiet minutes beforehand.
beats.good: She ate, read her notes once and walked out like she owned the hospital. Fingers crossed.
beats.bad: It was too busy for five quiet minutes. She went in flustered. 'I've done harder things on less sleep,' she said.

photo.caption: Interview notes, folded into a tiny square

beats.gossip: Good luck to a nurse from {district} with a big interview this week. She prepared over the {dish} at {restaurant}.

beats.order: {name} got the job. She's bringing her whole night shift in on {weekday}. Eight people. They want the {dish}.
beats.good: Eight nurses, one table, a lot of laughing about things we didn't understand. They left a card for the kitchen.

photo.caption: A thank-you card signed by a whole ward

beats.gossip: A whole night shift of nurses had dinner at {restaurant} on {weekday}. They left a thank-you card. We're not crying, you're crying.

beats.order: {name} has a rare weekend off and wants to do 'absolutely nothing' with the {dish} on {weekday}.
beats.good: She did absolutely nothing for two hours. She says it's the best two hours of her year.

photo.caption: Bola, feet up (on the chair opposite, sorry)

beats.gossip: A nurse from {district} sat at {restaurant} for two hours on {weekday} doing absolutely nothing. She's earned it.

beats.order: {name}'s mum is visiting from Lagos. {weekday}, the {dish}, and please be nice: she cooks better than anyone.
beats.good: Bola's mum tasted the {dish}, thought for a long time and said, 'Not bad.' Bola says that's practically a medal.

photo.caption: Bola's mum, inspecting the kitchen

beats.gossip: A visiting mum said 'not bad' about the {dish} at {restaurant}. Chefs on {district} are framing the quote.

regulars.name: Margaret Doyle
regulars.intro: Margaret did the crossword in ink, in nine minutes, and corrected the spelling on the specials board. Politely. Correctly.

beats.order: {name} has entered the county crossword championship. She trains over the {dish} on {weekday}.
beats.good: Two crosswords in the time it took to eat the {dish}. She's 'cautiously confident'. That means terrifyingly good.

photo.caption: A finished crossword, in pen, no crossings-out

beats.gossip: A retired teacher finished two crosswords at {restaurant} on {weekday}. In pen. Without asking anyone. Legend.

beats.order: {name} is through to the regional final. She'd like the {dish} on {weekday} and, quietly, a clue for nine across.
beats.good: Nine across was 'restaurant'. She got it from looking round. She says it's the easiest clue she's ever been given.
beats.bad: A noisy night put her off. She says she 'never loses her concentration'. She lost it on four down.

photo.caption: A regional finalist's badge, pinned to a cardigan

beats.gossip: {restaurant} has its own crossword champion. Well, finalist. Well, she eats here. Still counts.

beats.order: {name}'s old pupils have tracked her down. Six of them, {weekday}, the {dish}. She's pretending not to be thrilled.
beats.good: One of them is a doctor now, one's a pilot, and one is 'in crisps'. She remembered all their spellings.
beats.bad: Dinner was slow and she made them do a spelling test while they waited. They loved it, which is the worrying part.

photo.caption: An apple for the teacher, left on table two

beats.gossip: Six former pupils took their old teacher out to {restaurant} on {weekday}. She marked the menu. A-minus.

beats.order: The final is on {weekday}. {name} wants the {dish} afterwards, win or lose. (Win.)
beats.good: County crossword champion. She'd like everyone to know she didn't use a pencil once.

photo.caption: Champion. In ink.

beats.gossip: Margaret Doyle is county crossword champion and she celebrated at {restaurant}. Clue: rhymes with 'legend'. It's 'legend'.

regulars.name: Kai Thompson
regulars.intro: Kai tapped a rhythm on the table with two breadsticks for an hour. His band is called Hollow Spoons. Of course it is.

beats.order: Hollow Spoons have their first gig on {weekday}. {name} wants the {dish} for the whole band beforehand.
beats.good: They ate, they played, twelve people came. Eleven were family. One was the bin lorry driver. He danced.
beats.bad: Dinner ran late and they went on stage still chewing. The singer says it 'added texture'.

photo.caption: Two breadsticks, retired from drumming

beats.gossip: Local band Hollow Spoons played their first gig on {weekday}. The bin lorry driver was seen dancing. Of course he was.

beats.order: {name} wants to record a demo in the back room on {weekday}. Just kidding. He wants the {dish} and to talk about it a lot.
beats.good: They talked about the demo for three hours. They have a name for it: 'Pass the Salt'. No songs yet.

photo.caption: A set list on the back of a receipt

beats.gossip: Hollow Spoons' first demo will be called 'Pass the Salt'. It was planned at {restaurant}. It doesn't exist yet.

beats.order: Battle of the bands on {weekday}! {name} needs the {dish} 'for stamina'. The singer needs 'something soft for the voice'.
beats.good: Second place! The winners were a brass band of nine-year-olds. 'Fair,' said Kai. 'They were tight.'
beats.bad: They came last. The judges said 'loud'. Kai says loud is the point.

photo.caption: A runner-up rosette taped to a guitar

beats.gossip: Hollow Spoons came second at the battle of the bands, behind a brass band of nine-year-olds. Respect the brass.

beats.order: Hollow Spoons are supporting a real band on {weekday}. {name} wants the {dish} and to stop shaking.
beats.good: They played the big hall. They've written a song about {restaurant}. It's mostly about the {dish}. It slaps, apparently.

photo.caption: A gig poster: Hollow Spoons (small letters, still counts)

beats.gossip: Hollow Spoons have written a song about {restaurant}. Kai says it 'slaps'. We've been told that's good.

lines.waiting: Waiting for a {weekday} with the {dish} on and a good night (3.5★ or better).
lines.tryAgain: They came on {weekday} but it wasn't a good night. They'll try again next {weekday}.
lines.finished: Story complete. They're one of the family now.

thanks: Thanks for putting up with me. I'll be back next week, probably. Definitely. Probably.
You fed me through a strange year. I've told everyone. Well, two people. They're both coming.
Best table in {district}. Don't let anyone else sit at it. I'm only half joking.
I came in for the {dish} and stayed for the chaos in the kitchen. Ten out of ten. Would wait for a table again.
Thank you for remembering my order. Nobody else remembers anything about me. Not even my bank.
I've eaten at {restaurant} more times than I've eaten at home. My oven has started to take it personally.
You were there for every big moment. Mostly with gravy. That's what friends are for.
This is a thank-you note. I've never written one before. It's harder than it looks. Thank you.
If you ever take the {dish} off the menu, I will write a letter. A long one. In capitals.
Cheers for everything. I've left a tip and a slightly embarrassing amount of gratitude.
My mum says I talk about {restaurant} too much. My mum is wrong.
You made a regular out of someone who used to eat cereal for dinner. That's a public service.
Thanks for the food, the patience, and for pretending not to notice when I cried at the pudding.
Five stars. I'd give six, but apparently that's 'not how stars work'.
I'm not saying {restaurant} changed my life. I'm saying my life has a lot more {dish} in it now.
Thanks for every Friday. And the Tuesdays. And that one Sunday we don't talk about.
Keep the lights on. Somebody in {district} needs a place like this, and it's me.
Nobody asked for my review, so here it is anyway: you lot are brilliant. Don't let it go to your heads.
You never once rushed me out, even when I sat there for three hours with one coffee. Legends.
I'll still be here next week. You're stuck with me. Sorry. Not sorry.
Thank you. That's it. That's the note. I'm better at eating than writing.
